quick: 3.1 g (ticarcillin 3 g + clavulanate 0.1 g) every 4 to 6 hours
summary: Ticarcillin is a carboxypenicillin active against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, given with clavulanate. It was discontinued in the US (the label was withdrawn) and has largely been replaced by piperacillin-tazobactam.
indications: Serious infections due to susceptible Gram-negative organisms including Pseudomonas, intra-abdominal and soft-tissue infection (with clavulanate)

dosage.d: 3.1 g (ticarcillin 3 g + clavulanate 0.1 g) every 4 to 6 hours
CrCl 30 to 60: 2 g every 4 h; 10 to 30: 2 g every 8 h; under 10: 2 g every 12 h

admin: Use only as the finished product directs
moa: Binds penicillin-binding proteins, inhibiting cell-wall synthesis; clavulanate inhibits many beta-lactamases.

moderate: Aminoglycosides: in-vitro inactivation, do not mix in the same line

serious: Seizures at high dose in renal failure

counsel: Use exactly as the pack directs
Stop and seek care for rash, swelling or breathing difficulty
missed: Take it when remembered unless the next dose is due; do not double up.
overdose: No specific antidote. Supportive and symptomatic care.
